source_text:
καὶ πιστεύουσι μὲν 267 1 Kor 13,2–14,6 εἰς τὸ ἐλπίζειν, ἐλπίζουσι δὲ ἀναγκαία ἡ
ἀγάπη, ἵνα μὴ ἐκπέσωμεν τῆς ἐλπίδος. διὸ εἶπεν· μείζων τούτου ἡ ἀγάπη· διὰ γὰρ τῆς
ἀγάπης πληροῦται ὁ νόμος. 1 Kor 14,1–5 Ἐὰν γὰρ μὴ διερμηνεύῃ, μόνον δὲ λαλῇ
γλώσσῃ καὶ τὴν δύναμιν μὴ σαφανίζῃ ὡς οὐκ ἔχων τοῦτο τὸ τῆς διερμηνείας
χάρισμα, μυστήρια μὲν λαλεῖ–τὸ γὰρ πνεῦμα χορηγοῦν τὰς γλώσσας δηλονότι–καὶ
μυστήρια φθέγγεται διὰ τῶν γλωσσῶν, οὐκ οἰκοδομεῖ δὲ τὴν ἐκκλησίαν οὐκ
ἐπισταμένην ἃ λέγει. ὁ λαλῶν γλώσσῃ ἑαυτὸν οἰκοδομεῖ, ἐπιστάμενος ὅτι ἃ μὴ ἤδη
ἐφθέγγετο ἐνόει· πνεύματος ἁγίου ἦν χάρις ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ ᾠκοδομεῖτο. Ὥσπερ ὁ
γλώσσαις λαλῶν καὶ διερμηνεύοι, οὐκ ἔλαττόν ἐστι τοῦ προφήτου. Ζηλοῦτε, φησί,
πλείω τῶν ἄλλων χαρισμάτων τὴν προφητείαν. τοῦτο δὲ εἶπεν· πρὸς γὰρ τὴν
πολιτείαν ἑκάστου ἐδίδοτο τὰ χαρίσματα, καὶ ἐν αὐτοῖς ἦν ὃ ἤθελον ζηλῶσαι καὶ
λαβεῖν. ὅταν δὲ λαλῶσί τινες γλώσσαις, οὐδεὶς ἀκούων νοεῖ. ἀλλ' ὅμως εἰ καὶ τὰ
λαλούμενα ἄδηλα ἀνθρώποις, ἀλλ' ὁ ἐν πνεύματι λαλῶν λαλεῖ μυστήρια–τὸ γὰρ
πνεῦμα χορηγοῦν γλώσσαις μυστήρια φθέγγεται–, ὁ δὲ προφητεύων ὠφελεῖ τοὺς
ἀκούοντας· κατάδηλα γὰρ αὐτοῖς λαλεῖ. Μείζων ἡ χάρις, ἐὰν ὁ λαλῶν γλώσσαις καὶ
τὸ διερμηνεύειν λάβῃ· ἴσως γὰρ ὅτι ἀμφοτέρων οὐκ ἐτύγχανεν. Ὥσπερ ὁ γλώσσαις
λαλῶν καὶ διερμηνεύει, οὐκ ἔλαττόν ἐστι τοῦ προφήτου. 1 Kor 14,6 Τί ὑμᾶς
ὠφελήσω, φησίν, ἐὰν μὴ δύνωμαι ὑμῖν λαλεῖν ἢ περὶ ὧν ἀπεκαλύφθη μοι παρὰ
θεοῦ, ἢ περὶ ὧν αὐτὸς ἔγνων καὶ κατέλαβον, ἢ περὶ ὧν παρὰ προφήταις κατενόησα,
ἢ περὶ ὧν ὑμῖν συμβουλεύειν ἔγνωκα ἢ διδάσκειν; ἐὰν περὶ τούτων λαλῶ, ὑμεῖς δὲ
μὴ συνίετε, τί ὑμᾶς ὠφελήσω; 268 1 Kor 14,7 Σκοπεῖτε γάρ, φησίν, ὅτι καὶ ἐν τοῖς
ἀψύχοις αὐλῷ καὶ κιθάρᾳ ἐὰν μὴ διαστέλλωνται οἱ φθόγγοι, συγχεῖται τὸ
αὐλούμενον ἢ τὸ κιθαριζόμενον. 1 Kor 14,10 Οὐδὲν ἄφωνον, δηλονότι γένος
ἀνθρώπων. 1 Kor 14,12 Πνευματικὰ λαλεῖ τὰ διάφορα χαρίσματα τοῦ ἁγίου
πνεύματος. 1 Kor 14,13–14 Ἐάν, φησί, λαλήσω γλώσσῃ τινὶ ἣν οὐκ οἶδα, μηδὲ εἰδὼς
αὐτῆς τὴν δύναμιν, πέπεισμαι μὲν ὅτι νοῦν ἄκαρπον ἔχω οὐκ ἔχοντα τῶν εἰρημένων
τὴν δύναμιν. Προσευχέσθω ἵνα διπλῆς χάριτος τύχῃ, καὶ γλώσσαις λαλῇ καὶ ταύτας
ἑρμηνεύῃ. τὸ δὲ προσεύχεσθαι γλώσσῃ πνεύματος μὲν ἁγίου ἐστὶν ἐνέργεια, τοῦ δὲ
νοῦ ἀκαρπία γίνεται διὰ τὸ μηδένα δύνασθαι νοεῖν τὰ λεγόμενα ἢ ὠφελεῖσθαι. διό,
φησίν, τοῦτο ποιητέον μοι, σαφηνίζειν τὰ διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος χορηγούμενά μοι πρὸς
οἰκοδομὴν τῶν ἀκουόντων, ἵνα μὴ ὁ νοῦς ἄκαρπος ᾖ οὐκ ἔχων τῶν ῥημάτων τὴν
δύναμιν. 1 Kor 14,16 ∆ιὰ τὸ μηδένα δύνασθαι ὠφελεῖσθαι ἢ συνιέναι τὰ λεγόμενα,
ἐὰν εὐχαριστῶ γλώττῃ, οὐκ ἀποδίδωσί σοι ὁ ἀκροατὴς τὸ ἀμήν. ἰδιώτην δὲ λέγει
ὥσπερ τὸν ἀστράτευτον τὸν μηδέπω βαπτισθέντα. 1 Kor 14,19 Τῇ σαφηνείᾳ τοῦ νοῦ
καὶ τῇ συνήθει γλώττῃ. 1 Kor 14, Τέλειοι γίνεσθαι σπουδάζετε, νοεῖν τὰς γραφάς. 269
1 Kor 14,21–23 Ἐπισημήνασθαι χρὴ ὅτι ἀπαιτούμενοι Ἰουδαῖοι, ὅπου ὁ θεὸς ἐν
πολλαῖς αὐταῖς ἐλάλησε γλώσσαις κἀκεῖνοι ἠπείθησαν, οὐκ ἔχουσι δεῖξαι· ἡμεῖς δὲ
δείκνυμεν ὅτι, ὅτε ἦλθε. τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον καὶ ἐμέρισεν γλώσσαις, οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι
ἀπειθοῦντες ἔλεγον· γλεύκους μεμεστωμένοι εἰσίν. ὥστε αἱ γλῶσσαι εἰς σημεῖόν
εἰσιν οὐ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἀλλὰ τοῖς ἀπίστοις, ἡ δὲ προφητεία οὐ τοῖς ἀπίστοις ἀλλὰ
τοῖς πιστεύουσιν. ὥστε οἰκοδομοῦσιν αἱ γλῶσσαι, ὅταν μάθῃ ὁ ἀκούων ὅτι ὁ λαλῶν
λαλεῖ γλῶσσαν ἣν οὐκ οἶδεν, οὐ μὴν οἰκοδομὴν λαμβάνει τῆς ὠφελείας τῆς
πνευματικῆς διδαχῆς διὰ τὸ μὴ νοεῖσθαι μὴ προχωρούσης· ἡ μὲν γὰρ προφητεία
μελλόντων, τοῖς δὲ περὶ τούτων λεγομένοις ὁ τυχὼν οὐ πιστεύει ἀλλ' ὁ πιστός. ὁ δὲ
ἄπιστος χρείαν ἔχει τοῦ οὐκ εἰδότος τὴν γλῶσσαν ᾗ κέχρηται, καὶ δεικνύντος ὅτι
θεοῦ πνεῦμα ἐν αὐτῷ. ὥστε θαῦμα ἦν ἡ γλῶττα, ἡ δὲ προφητεία ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκβάσεως
θαῦμα, οὐκ ἐν τῷ λέγεσθαι. διχῶς δὲ λέγεται ἀπιστία ἐν τῇ θείᾳ γραφῇ· καὶ ἡ ἀληθῶς
ἀπιστία ἡ τῶν Ἑλλήνων, καὶ ἡ ὀλιγοπιστία ἡ τῶν εὐσεβῶν. Ἄπιστον λέγει τὸν
Ἕλληνα, ἰδιώτην δὲ τὸν μήπω βα270 πτισθέντα, τὸν ἀστράτευτον· τότε γὰρ οὐκ
ἐλέγοντο κατηχούμενοι ἢ ἀβάπτιστοι. 269,ξολ2 Νόμον λέγει καὶ τὰ τῶν ἄλλων
προφητῶν, ἐπειδὴ κατὰ νόμον ἐπολιτεύοντο. τὸ δὲ εἰρημένον τῷ Ἡσαΐᾳ τότε ἀπέβη
ὅτε κατῆλθεν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀποστόλους τὸ πνεῦμα, καὶ ἐλάλουν γλώσσαις καὶ ἐχλεύαζον
Ἰουδαῖοι. ∆ηλονότι ὠφελοῦσιν αἱ γλῶσσαι, ὅταν ὁ ἀκούων γνῶ ὅτι ὁ λαλῶν γλώσσῃ
λαλεῖ ἣν οὐκ οἶδεν οὐδ' ἔμαθεν παρ' ἀνθρώπων, ὅμως οὐκ ὠφελεῖ τὸ πρᾶγμα τὸν
pass_a_gloss: [13:13 note, continued] And to those believing [it is] for hoping, and to those hoping love is necessary, so that we may not fall out of hope. Therefore he said: 'greater than this is love'; for through love the law is fulfilled. [Page 267 running head '1 Kor 13,2-14,6' inside the sentence; not printed.] [Label 1 Kor 14,1-5] For if he does not interpret, but only speaks in a tongue and does not make clear the meaning, as not having this gift of interpretation, he speaks mysteries (clearly the Spirit supplying the tongues [does]) and utters mysteries through the tongues, but he does not build up the church, which does not understand what he says. The one speaking in a tongue builds himself up, knowing that he was uttering things he did not know (Greek ἤδη, read ᾔδει); he perceived [that] the grace of the Holy Spirit was in him, and he was built up. So (Greek Ὥσπερ) if the one speaking in tongues also interprets, he is not less than the prophet. 'Be zealous', he says, 'for prophecy more than the other gifts.' And he said this: for the gifts were given according to the way of life of each, and it was in them [to choose] what they wished to be zealous for and to receive. And when some speak in tongues, no one hearing understands. But nevertheless, even if the things spoken are unclear to people, still the one speaking in the Spirit speaks mysteries (for the Spirit supplying tongues utters mysteries), but the one prophesying benefits those hearing; for he speaks plainly to them. The grace is greater if the one speaking in tongues receives also the interpreting; for perhaps [it was] that he did not have both. [Exact repeat, not printed again: So if the one speaking in tongues also interprets, he is not less than the prophet.] [Label 1 Kor 14,6] What will I benefit you, he says, if I am not able to speak to you either about the things revealed to me from God, or about the things I myself knew and grasped, or about the things I understood in the prophets, or about the things I have decided to counsel or teach you? If I speak about these, but you do not understand, what will I benefit you? [Label 1 Kor 14,7] For look, he says, that even in lifeless things, flute and lyre, if the sounds are not distinguished, the piped or harped [tune] is confused. [Label 1 Kor 14,10] Nothing voiceless: clearly, race of men. [Label 1 Kor 14,12] He calls spiritual things the different gifts of the Holy Spirit. [Label 1 Kor 14,13-14] If, he says, I speak in some tongue which I do not know, not even knowing its meaning, I am persuaded that I have an unfruitful mind, not having the meaning of the things said. Let him pray that he may obtain a double grace, both to speak in tongues and to interpret them. And to pray in a tongue is a working of the Holy Spirit, but unfruitfulness of the mind comes about because no one can understand the things said or benefit. Therefore, he says, this must be done by me, to make clear the things supplied to me through the Spirit toward the building up of the hearers, so that the mind may not be unfruitful, not having the meaning of the words. [Label 1 Kor 14,16] Because no one can benefit or understand the things said, if I give thanks in a tongue, the hearer does not give back to you the amen. And he calls 'private person' as it were the unenlisted, the one not yet baptized. [Label 1 Kor 14,19] With the clarity of the mind and with the customary tongue. [Label 1 Kor 14, (verse missing)] Be eager to become mature, to understand the Scriptures. [Page 269; label 1 Kor 14,21-23] One must note that Jews, being challenged [to show] where God spoke to them in many tongues and they disobeyed, are not able to show [it]; but we show that when the Holy Spirit came and divided in tongues, the Jews, disbelieving, said: 'they are filled with new wine.' So tongues are for a sign not to those believing but to the unbelieving, and prophecy not to the unbelieving but to those believing. So tongues build up, when the hearer learns that the one speaking speaks a tongue which he does not know, yet he does not receive the building up of the benefit of the spiritual teaching because of not being understood, not going forward; for prophecy is of things to come, and in the things said about these not the chance person believes but the believer. And the unbeliever has need of one not knowing the tongue which he uses and showing that God's Spirit is in him. So the tongue was a wonder, and prophecy a wonder from the outcome, not in being said. And unbelief is said in two ways in the divine Scripture: both the true unbelief, that of the Greeks, and the little faith, that of the devout. He calls the Greek unbeliever, and private person the one not yet baptized, the unenlisted; for then they were not called catechumens or unbaptized. [Second form, 269 col2] He calls law also the [writings] of the other prophets, since they lived according to law. And the thing said by Isaiah came about then when the Spirit came down on the apostles, and they spoke in tongues and Jews mocked. Clearly the tongues benefit when the hearer knows that the one speaking in a tongue speaks one which he does not know nor learned from people, yet the thing does not benefit the... [continues]
pass_b_english: And believers believe so that they may hope, and those who hope need love, so that we do not fall away from hope. That is why he said, “Greater than this is love,” for it is through love that the law is fulfilled.

On 1 Corinthians 14:1–5: If he does not interpret, but only speaks in a tongue and does not make its meaning clear, because he lacks this gift of interpretation, he does speak mysteries (that is, clearly, the Spirit who supplies the tongues does) and he utters mysteries through the tongues. But he does not build up the church, which does not understand what he is saying. The one who speaks in a tongue builds himself up, knowing that he is uttering what he did not know; he perceived that the grace of the Holy Spirit was in him, and he was built up. So if the one who speaks in tongues also interprets, he is not less than the prophet.

“Be eager,” he says, “for prophecy more than the other gifts.” He said this because the gifts were given to match each person's way of life, and it was up to them which gift they wished to be eager for and receive. When some speak in tongues, no one who hears understands. Even so, though what is spoken is unclear to people, the one who speaks in the Spirit speaks mysteries (for the Spirit who supplies the tongues utters mysteries), while the one who prophesies helps those who hear, because he speaks to them plainly. The grace is greater if the one who speaks in tongues also receives the gift of interpreting; perhaps it was that he did not have both.

On 1 Corinthians 14:6: What good will I do you, he says, if I cannot speak to you about what was revealed to me by God, or about what I myself have come to know and grasp, or about what I have understood in the prophets, or about what I have resolved to counsel or teach you? If I speak about these things and you do not understand, what good will I do you?
On 1 Corinthians 14:7: Consider, he says, that even with lifeless things, the flute and the lyre, if the notes are not distinct, what is piped or played becomes a blur.
On 1 Corinthians 14:10: “Nothing is without voice”: that is, clearly, no race of men.
On 1 Corinthians 14:12: By “spiritual things” he means the different gifts of the Holy Spirit.

On 1 Corinthians 14:13–14: If, he says, I speak in some tongue that I do not know, without even knowing what it means, I am persuaded that my mind is unfruitful, since it does not have the meaning of what was said. Let him pray to obtain a double grace: to speak in tongues and to interpret them. Praying in a tongue is the working of the Holy Spirit, but the mind bears no fruit, because no one can understand what is said or benefit from it. That is why, he says, I must do this: make clear what the Spirit supplies to me, to build up those who hear, so that my mind is not unfruitful for want of the meaning of the words.

On 1 Corinthians 14:16: Because no one can benefit from what is said or understand it, if I give thanks in a tongue, the listener does not give you back the “Amen.” By “outsider” he means one who, so to speak, has not yet enlisted: one not yet baptized.
On 1 Corinthians 14:19: With the clarity of the mind, and in the ordinary language.
On 1 Corinthians 14:20: Be eager to become mature: to understand the Scriptures.

On 1 Corinthians 14:21–23: Note this. When the Jews are asked to show where God spoke to them in many tongues and they disobeyed, they cannot show it. But we show that when the Holy Spirit came and made the division into tongues, the Jews in their disbelief said, “They are full of new wine” (Acts 2:13). So tongues are a sign not for believers but for unbelievers, and prophecy is not for unbelievers but for believers. Tongues do build up, then, when the hearer learns that the speaker is speaking a language he does not know; yet he does not receive the building up that comes from the benefit of spiritual teaching, since it is not understood and makes no headway. Prophecy concerns things to come, and it is not just anyone who believes what is said about them, but the believer. The unbeliever needs a man who does not know the language he is using, and who so shows that the Spirit of God is in him. So the tongue was a wonder, while prophecy was a wonder by its fulfillment, not in the speaking. Divine Scripture speaks of unbelief in two ways: the true unbelief of the Greeks, and the little faith of the devout. By “unbeliever” he means the Greek, and by “outsider” the one not yet baptized, the one not yet enlisted; at that time they were not called catechumens or unbaptized.

The second catena form adds: He calls the writings of the other prophets “law” too, since they lived under the law. What was spoken through Isaiah (Isaiah 28:11) came to pass when the Spirit came down on the apostles and they spoke in tongues and the Jews mocked. choices.english: uttering what he did not know; he perceived
choices.why: ἤδη read as ᾔδει (itacism, same sound); punctuation moved before ἐνόει. Noted.

choices.term: Ὥσπερ ὁ γλώσσαις λαλῶν καὶ διερμηνεύοι
choices.english: So if the one who speaks in tongues also interprets
choices.why: Optative/indicative after Ὥσπερ only makes sense as a condition; read as result 'so if'.
